name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+8 district with a favorable national environment for Democrats
Cisneros holds a massive fundraising advantage ($705K vs $82K)
Prediction markets price Cisneros at ~95% to win
No public polling, but challenger Eric Ching is little-known and underfunded
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Cisneros: a D+8 seat, a pro-Democratic environment, incumbency, and a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge. Markets agree at about 95%, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin with only a slight trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending for Ching or a shift in the national environment could narrow what is currently a lopsided picture.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gil Cisneros, the Democratic incumbent, is favored to hold a Southern California seat that leans Democratic by eight points. He has raised about $705,000 to challenger Eric Ching's $82,000 and holds a large cash advantage, with modest outside support on his side and none against him. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters list the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets put Cisneros's chances around 95%, consistent with a comfortable but not automatic win. The forecast expects a Democratic margin near nineteen points, with uncertainty somewhat elevated because direct polling evidence is absent.
